customer_acme_ops: Hey team — our batch rerank returned scores but they're not aligned with per-query candidate lists. Request ID 01ABCD. Appears shifted by one when we bulk-uploaded a CSV.

emma: Sorry about that — can you paste the sanitized request body you sent and the top of the response? Which client/version are you using?

customer_acme_ops: Using our internal uploader (python) v0.3. Sent JSON via the /v1/rerank/batch endpoint. Here's a sanitized snippet we used:
```json
{
  "queries": ["How to reset password","Cancel subscription"],
  "per_query_candidates": [
    ["Reset steps A","Reset steps B"],
    ["Cancel policy A","Cancel policy B"]
  ]
}
```
But response flattened scores: [0.92,0.15,0.34,0.81] and the mapping seems to apply the first two scores to the first query only.

ravi: Two quick possibilities: 1) the server parsed payload as flat candidates (legacy mode) because field name mismatch, or 2) CSV ingestion created a candidate spillover due to embedded newline/quoting.

sam: Can you share the raw CSV you used to upload? We saw a recent customer case where a quoted candidate cell had an embedded newline which merged rows on ingest. Also check Content-Type when uploading.

customer_acme_ops: Attached raw CSV lines: 
```
"How to reset password","\"Reset steps A
with extra line\";Reset steps B"
"Cancel subscription","Cancel policy A;Cancel policy B"
```
They used semicolons as candidate separators inside the cell. The uploader converted to JSON and sent `per_query_candidates` but maybe parser mis-handled the newline.

emma: I repro'd this in the UI by uploading the same CSV; got the same offset. Created internal ticket RERANK-321. Logs show: `parseCandidates: fallback=flat_mode` then `assignOffsets: bucket_shift=+1` around 2024-06-15T12:04:23Z. That looks like our CSV parser detected inconsistent quoting and fell back.

ravi: If the parser falls back to flat mode it flattens all candidates into one stream, then slices per query using counts — if counts are off because of row merging, offsets will shift. The embedded newline inside a quoted cell is the usual culprit.

sam: Also observed a latency spike because the parser retried the ingestion path a few times; we saw 500s for those requests and several retries landed on billing. cc @billing-team.

emma: Immediate mitigation: 1) re-upload CSV with embedded newlines escaped or remove newlines, 2) send the payload explicitly as JSON with `per_query_candidates` inlined (bypass CSV path), or 3) use the uploader flag `--csv-quoting=double` to force strict parsing.

customer_acme_ops: For workaround we re-sent as JSON and alignment restored. Can you please confirm we won't be charged for the failed retries? Our monthly usage jumped.

emma: Please DM me the account id and the list of request ids showing retries. We'll audit and credit obviously-broken retries once we confirm scope.

logging-bot: deploy-started r10.14 to prod on eng-infra at 2024-06-17T03:22:10Z

ravi: For long-term fix I'm going to harden the CSV parser: stricter quote validation, explicit rejection (400) for ambiguous CSVs instead of fallback, and unit tests for multiline quoted cells. I'll also add an ingest-time warning in the UI explaining candidate separators and quoting rules.

sam: Side task: add a monitoring alert for `assignOffsets.bucket_shift != 0` spikes to catch regressions early.

emma: We've marked the support thread as escalated and assigned to eng-ml (ravi) and eng-infra (sam). ETA for parser fix: 72 hours. We'll push a hotfix to reject ambiguous CSVs sooner to avoid silent misalignments.

customer_acme_ops: Thanks, that path forward sounds good. DMed the request ids. Appreciate the quick turnaround. :pray:

emma: Thanks — we'll follow up in the ticket and update you when credits are applied. Marking thread tentatively resolved until the patch lands. :white_check_mark:
